subject: Warm-pool quota top-up and pricing terms
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@observa.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Warm-pool quota top-up for end-of-quarter surge

Hi Avery / Sergio,

Quick note — we're seeing a predictable traffic spike the last week of April tied to a new partner rollout. Our engineers estimate a ~3x increase in inference volume for a 10-day window (roughly Apr 24–May 3).

Can Redwood offer a short-term "warm-pool" or quota top-up so we can handle the burst without hitting hard rate limits? We're primarily interested in:
- A temporary token/day uplift (preferably a fixed warm pool capacity we can hit immediately)
- A clear pricing structure (flat burst fee vs per-token overage)
- Any credit or discount if we commit to a short-term reserved warm pool

If you can share a proposal today or tomorrow that includes estimated cost and any contract amendment required, that would be ideal — procurement is on a tight timeline. I've attached our March usage export for reference.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Observa AI
[Attachment: observa-usage-march-2027.csv (CSV)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@observa.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Warm-pool quota top-up for end-of-quarter surge

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the usage export. Wanted to outline a pragmatic option that is quick to stand up and minimizes billing surprises for Observa. See summary below; I attached a short one-page proposal.

Proposal (warm-pool top-up, short-term):
- Duration: 14 days (configurable; default Apr 24–May 7)
- Capacity: Warm pool sized at 500k tokens/day (immediately available, no cold-start)
- Billing: flat daily burst unit at $120/day covering up to the 500k token allotment; per-token overrun beyond the pool billed at $0.0009/token
- One-time setup: $500 (restarts, routing)
- Introductory credit: 20% credit against the first invoice for customers committing to the 14-day window within 48 hours of this email
- Safeguard: automatic soft-throttling if daily usage exceeds 2x the pool to prevent runaway invoices; Redwood will notify Observa 1 hour before throttle.

If Observa wants a deeper discount in exchange for a short-term commit and a post-event usage review, we can propose a tiered discount (see attached PDF v2).

Next steps:
1) Confirm dates and capacity (reply to this thread)
2) I'll have Legal/Finance prepare an amendment and a DocuSign link (we can waive the $500 setup if Observa accepts the 20% introductory credit)

Attaching: Observa-WarmPool-Proposal-v2.pdf

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Observa-WarmPool-Proposal-v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Procurement <procurement@observa.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@observa.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Warm-pool quota top-up for end-of-quarter surge

Avery — thanks, that layout helps. A few procurement items we'd need to confirm before we can sign an amendment: 

1) Formal quote on company letterhead with total not-to-exceed amount for the 14-day window (including setup).
2) Confirmation: will unused daily warm pool capacity roll over to the following day during the window, or is it per-day consumption only?
3) SLA / availability: what uptime guarantee applies to the warm pool and what credits (if any) would apply for service degradation during the committed period?
4) Invoice and payment terms (Net 30 is our default) and whether the 20% introductory credit is itemized on invoice.
5) If Observa underutilizes the pool by >70% across the 14 days, is there a prorated credit or backward-looking rebate?

We can expedite on our side if Legal receives a draft amendment with the quote and basic terms.

Procurement
Observa AI

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Observa warm-pool negotiation strategy

Avery — quick thoughts after reviewing Elena's usage file and procurement asks. Key negotiation levers: a) introductory credit vs. b) capped not-to-exceed amount and c) rollback clause for underutilization.

I recommend the following, to balance risk and close quickly: 
- Offer a formal quote with a not-to-exceed cap equal to (14 * $120) + $500 = $2,180, with the 20% introductory credit applied on the first invoice (so effective cap $1,744). That gives Observa cost certainty which procurement likes.
- Rollover: allow unused daily capacity to roll forward within the 14-day window but not beyond. This reduces their risk of wasted capacity.
- Underutilization rebate: if Observa uses <30% of reserved tokens over the window, apply a 50% rebate on the setup fee only (not on daily units). Keeps us from setting a precedent of full refunds.
- SLA: our warm-pool is a soft-availability construct; offer 99.5% availability and a 10% credit on daily fees for any day with >60 minutes of warm-pool unavailability. Legal can vet tighter language.
- Auto-throttle thresholds: keep the 2x soft-throttle but cap emergency overrun at 1M tokens/day at the per-token overrun price; anything beyond that requires explicit approval.

I've attached a redlined quote (WarmPool-Quote-Redline.xlsx) with the not-to-exceed figures and suggested invoice language. If we present the not-to-exceed and rollover terms up-front, procurement typically signs quickly.

Sergio
Head of Sales, West
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: WarmPool-Quote-Redline.xlsx (XLSX)]

Subject: Re: Request: Warm-pool quota top-up for end-of-quarter surge

Hi Procurement / Elena — thanks for the prompt feedback and the clear asks. Per Sergio's recommendation, we've prepared a not-to-exceed quote and included the requested rollover and SLA language. Key points: 

- Not-to-exceed: $1,744 (after 20% introductory credit) for the 14-day window if Observa signs the amendment by Apr 14 12:00 PT.
- Rollover: unused daily capacity rolls forward within the 14-day window only.
- Underutilization rebate: 50% refund of the $500 setup fee if total utilization <30% across the window.
- SLA credit: 10% of daily fees for days with >60 minutes of warm-pool unavailability; Redwood will proactively notify and credit Observa.
- DocuSign: Legal has prepared the amendment and a DocuSign link will be sent after you confirm acceptance. We can set invoice terms to Net 30.

Next steps for Observa to accept: reply with a confirmation of the dates and sign via DocuSign when it arrives. If you'd prefer, I can convert the not-to-exceed quote into a pro-forma invoice so procurement has a single document for routing.

If we don't receive a signed amendment by Apr 14 12:00 PT, the introductory 20% credit will no longer be guaranteed. Happy to hop on a 15-minute call if you want to walk through any details.

Best,
